sections.h2: Selling a house in Clarksville, TN
sections.html:
Montgomery County's seat sits roughly ten miles from Fort Campbell, home of the 101st Airborne Division. About 188,829 people lived in Clarksville on July 1, 2025, up 13.2 percent from April 2020.

Of all homes, 55.6 percent are owner occupied, with a typical value of $263,600, and rent typically runs $1,307. A seller with permanent change of station orders may have a firm report date, and speed then outweighs squeezing out the last few thousand dollars.

A cash purchase on an as-is basis removes repair negotiation, showings and buyer financing from that clock. A conventional listing works when the house is move-in ready and the move date is flexible.

Buyers remember damaging weather here. A tornado ranked F3 hit downtown in January 1999, an EF2 struck the east side in February 2018, and floods damaged the city in May 2010. In December 2023 an EF3 tornado crossed North Clarksville.

What this means in practice for a seller:

  • Keep roof, siding and window receipts, and note any insurance claim paid for storm damage.
  • Keep permits for repairs made after a storm, since a buyer's inspector will compare work to paperwork.
  • If the house was damaged and not fully repaired, describe the condition to buyers in writing and consider an as-is sale.
  • Check the flood risk for low lots near the Red River and Cumberland River before setting a price.

Cash buyers price the repairs they find, so an honest description up front speeds an offer.

sections.h2: How Clarksville property taxes are billed and paid
sections.html:
Clarksville and Montgomery County send separate bills. The city builds its bills from the county assessor's file, and that file names whoever held title on January 1. Notices mail in October, payment is accepted from October 1 until the final day of February, and later payments carry interest of 1.5 percent a month, which is 18 percent a year.

Read your closing documents to see who owes the taxes, because a property can still go to a tax auction if the taxes stay unpaid, whoever was supposed to pay. After a year of delinquency the city turns the account over to a delinquent tax attorney, and payments are then made at the Clerk and Master's office in Montgomery Chancery Court at 2 Millennium Plaza, Number 101.

Payment options at the city level are:

  • In person at Finance and Revenue, One Public Square, Suite 119.
  • At the North Center, 111 Cunningham Lane.
  • By mail to P.O. Box 30549, Clarksville, TN 37040, with the bill stub.
  • Online, which carries a 2.5 percent processing fee.

If a lender and an owner both pay, the city refunds the party that paid second. Call 931-645-7436 with questions. Ask Finance and Revenue at 931-645-7437 for the current city rate.

Clarksville offers two kinds of relief: one for elderly or disabled homeowners and one for disabled former service members and their surviving spouses. A first-time applicant signs up at the Montgomery County Trustee or at the City of Clarksville Finance and Revenue office, not both. The Trustee is at 350 Pageant Lane, Suite 101-B, phone 931-648-5717.

Those approved for the age or disability category receive a voucher each year with the county and city bills and must bring income records to the city. Recipients in the service-member category send signed vouchers to both the city and the county. The state remits its share only when those vouchers come in.

The same Trustee office handles the Tax Freeze program, and the county notifies the city of an approved freeze. Ask the Trustee which documents each program requires before you apply.

sections.h2: Which Clarksville home rules can delay a sale?
sections.html:
City codes matter when an inspection turns up violations. The Codes Enforcement Division reviews property maintenance rules, takes complaints and offers a housing inspection request form. Vehicles may not park on grass and must sit on concrete, asphalt or gravel. A fence taller than six feet needs a permit, and fences on a residential lot follow 30 or 40 foot front setbacks.

Pools get particular attention from inspectors. Outdoor residential pools need a barrier no lower than 48 inches, gates that close and latch themselves, and openings that stop a 4-inch sphere. Check an older pool and any fence near the setback line against these rules before a buyer's inspector does.

To confirm a lot's zoning, call Building and Codes at 931-645-7426, and call the Regional Planning Commission at 931-645-7448 about rezoning. Close any open complaint before listing, and keep the paperwork that shows it was resolved. A buyer's lender may ask for it, and a cash buyer will want to know nothing is outstanding.

sections.h2: Recording the deed and what it costs
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Montgomery County Register of Deeds, 350 Pageant Lane, Suite 101-A, phone 931-648-5713, where weekday hours run from 7:30 am to 4:30 pm. The office cannot prepare documents or run title searches. It requires original signed and notarized documents, wants the name and address of whoever prepared the deed, and requires an oath of consideration on transfers unless a statute exempts the instrument.

Clarksville recording charges
ChargeAmount
State transfer tax37 cents for each $100 of price
Mortgage tax11.5 cents on each $100 of debt after the first $2,000
Copies$0.15 per page; certified $1.00 per page
Payment typesCash, check with ID, money order, card with a fee

The title company totals the recording costs and delivers the signed deed to the office. Because the office will not prepare your deed or search title, make sure the title company or an attorney handles both before the closing date.

Gather a lender payoff statement, your deed and a list of every co-owner. Every owner signs before a notary, so confirm early who will be at the table. Check your latest city and county tax bills, and ask Finance and Revenue what remains unpaid.

If title is clear, a cash buyer can close on a date you pick, often about two weeks away, and a written closing date helps you plan around your report date. On closing day the title company divides the year's tax with the buyer, totals the recording costs and sends the deed in.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Clarksville house quickly if I have PCS orders?
faqs.a: Yes. Have a payoff statement, the deed and co-owner details ready.

faqs.q: Who pays Clarksville property tax at closing?
faqs.a: The contract decides the split, and the title company shows it on the closing statement. Since the city bill goes to the January 1 owner, read your closing papers to learn who actually sends payment. Unpaid taxes can end in a tax auction.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed for a Clarksville house?
faqs.a: The Montgomery County Register of Deeds, 350 Pageant Lane, Suite 101-A, phone 931-648-5713. Originals with signatures and notary acknowledgments are required, plus the oath of consideration on most transfers.

faqs.q: What does the state charge on a Clarksville home sale?
faqs.a: Tennessee charges 37 cents on each $100 of price as realty transfer tax. Secured debt above the first $2,000 also owes an 11.5 cent mortgage tax per $100. Both show up on the closing statement.

faqs.q: Is there property tax relief for Clarksville seniors?
faqs.a: Yes. The city and county offer relief for elderly and disabled homeowners and for disabled former service members, plus the Tax Freeze program. Apply at the Montgomery County Trustee, 931-648-5717, or at City Finance and Revenue, 931-645-7436, but not at both.
